scheme_name: Promotion of Acting in Tiatr for School Children
description:
The "Promotion of Acting in Tiatr for School Children" scheme is an initiative launched by the Government of Goa in 2018. 

The scheme aims to promote the traditional art form of Tiatr among school children. 

Tiatr is a popular form of musical theatre in Goa that combines drama, music, and dance. 

The objective of this scheme is to encourage creativity and artistic expression among the youth. 

The government seeks to instill a sense of cultural pride and heritage through this initiative. 

The scheme targets school children aged between 6 to 18 years. 

It aims to involve students from both government and private schools across Goa. 

The program is designed to enhance the skills of children in acting, singing, and stage performance. 

The government has set a target to train at least 1,000 students annually under this scheme. 

The training sessions are conducted by experienced Tiatr artists and professionals. 

The government provides financial assistance for organizing workshops and training sessions. 

Each workshop can receive a grant of up to ₹50,000. 

This financial support is aimed at covering expenses related to materials, venue, and artist fees. 

The scheme also encourages schools to organize Tiatr competitions. 

These competitions provide a platform for students to showcase their talents. 

The winners of these competitions receive cash prizes and certificates. 

The cash prizes can range from ₹5,000 to ₹20,000 depending on the level of the competition. 

The scheme also includes provisions for organizing Tiatr festivals. 

These festivals are aimed at promoting the art form and providing exposure to young talents. 

The government allocates a budget of ₹10 lakh annually for the promotion of these festivals. 

Eligibility for participation in the scheme requires students to be enrolled in a recognized school in Goa. 

There are no specific income criteria for students to participate. 

However, preference is given to students from economically weaker sections. 

The application process for schools involves submitting a proposal to the Directorate of Art and Culture. 

The proposal must include details about the planned activities and the number of students involved. 

Schools must also provide a list of qualified trainers or artists who will conduct the sessions. 

Once the proposal is approved, schools can begin organizing workshops and competitions. 

The Directorate of Art and Culture reviews the proposals and disburses funds accordingly. 

The timeline for the application process typically starts in June each year. 

Schools are encouraged to submit their proposals by the end of July. 

The workshops and training sessions usually take place from August to December. 

Competitions are held in January and February to coincide with the Tiatr festival season. 

The government collaborates with various cultural organizations to implement this scheme. 

The Goa Tiatr Academy is one of the key partners in promoting this initiative. 

They provide expertise in organizing events and training sessions. 

The Directorate of Art and Culture is the primary implementing authority for this scheme. 

They are responsible for monitoring the progress and impact of the initiative. 

Contact details for the Directorate of Art and Culture can be found on the official Goa government website. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from schools and parents alike. 

Many students have reported increased confidence and improved public speaking skills. 

The initiative has also led to a revival of interest in Tiatr among younger generations. 

Statistics indicate that participation in Tiatr-related activities has increased by 30% since the launch of the scheme. 

The government aims to expand the program to include more schools in rural areas. 

This expansion is part of a broader strategy to promote cultural education in Goa. 

The scheme aligns with the government's vision of preserving and promoting Goan culture. 

It also complements other educational initiatives aimed at holistic development. 

Overall, the "Promotion of Acting in Tiatr for School Children" scheme is a significant step towards fostering artistic talent among the youth. 

It provides a structured approach to learning and appreciating the rich cultural heritage of Goa. 

By investing in the arts, the government is nurturing a generation that values creativity and expression. 

This initiative is expected to have long-term benefits for both the students and the cultural landscape of Goa. 

The scheme represents a commitment to cultural education and community engagement. 

It is an example of how government initiatives can effectively support traditional art forms. 

As the program continues to evolve, it is likely to adapt to the changing needs of students and the community. 

The success of this scheme could serve as a model for similar initiatives in other states. 

By focusing on youth engagement in the arts, the government is paving the way for a vibrant cultural future. 

In conclusion, the "Promotion of Acting in Tiatr for School Children" scheme is a comprehensive initiative that addresses multiple aspects of cultural education. 

It provides financial support, training, and opportunities for young talents to shine. 

The scheme not only promotes Tiatr but also contributes to the overall development of students in Goa. 

With ongoing support and participation, this initiative has the potential to leave a lasting impact on the cultural fabric of the region.
